result.title: Do large language models rank moral values? A transitivity test of moral competence
result.summary: LLMs are increasingly used to support decisions that require moral consideration. While LLMs perform well on morality benchmarks from psychology and philosophy, producing appropriate outputs on these benchmarks (moral performance) does not establish that an LLM weighs competing moral values at stake in a decision (moral competence). We test a minimal, necessary condition for such weighing: that an ordinal ranking can represent LLM moral choices. Such a ranking requires transitivity. To assess transitivity, we presented LLMs with pairwise trade-offs among moral value violations in vignette choice sets and extracted resulting choice probabilities from first-token distributions. Tested against three stochastic transitive choice models, most choice sets admitted weak or unstable orderings. Aggregating an LLM's responses, a common practice in LLM moral evaluation, produced transitive structure that matched no individual choice set. Evaluations of AI morality should establish that choices are structured before asking whether they are aligned.

AI.brief_summary: 论文检验 LLM 道德能力的最小必要条件：从情境权衡题的首 token 分布提取成对选择概率，用三种随机传递选择模型检验其序数排序是否满足传递性，发现多数选择集只支持弱或不稳定的排序，且跨响应聚合出的传递结构不对应任何单个选择集。
AI.relevance_reason: 从首 token 概率重建选择并做传递性/一致性检验、以及指出聚合会掩盖单个实例的结构，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否支持一致的序数比较，以及推理评价中跨样本聚合的风险。
